facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia
prostate-specific antigen level was 0.796 ng/mL
Uroflowmetry revealed reduced urine flow, prolonged micturition time, and obstructive findings
He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily
loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
no history of liver disease
leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL
total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL (0.2–1.2)
Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts
